mechanism.plausibility_rationale: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors like acarbose are primarily used for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes. While some studies have suggested potential cardiovascular benefits due to improved postprandial glucose levels, there is no established direct causal mechanism linking the inhibition of carbohydrate digestion to the induction of myocardial infarction. In fact, clinical evidence generally points toward a neutral or slightly protective effect on cardiovascular outcomes rather than an increased risk.
